hero.heading: Learn how the platform works before you begin.
hero.description: TradeIQ helps you explore the Colombo Stock Exchange, test investing rules on historical prices, and practise trades with virtual money. It is a research and learning workspace, not a broker or investment adviser.

capabilities.heading: Explore. Test. Practise. Review.
capabilities.description: Each part of TradeIQ answers a different question. You can begin with public market browsing, then use the simulation tools when you are ready.

markets.title: Explore market data
markets.description: Search CSE-listed companies, compare the latest available end-of-day prices, filter by sector, and open historical price charts. Public market browsing does not require an account.

backtesting.title: Backtest an idea
backtesting.description: Choose a security and apply defined buy and sell rules to past prices. The simulation can include starting cash, trading costs, and risk limits so you can review how those rules behaved historically.

paperTrading.title: Practise paper trading
paperTrading.description: Place simulated buy and sell orders using virtual cash. Paper trading lets you learn the order workflow and observe the result without sending an order to a real exchange or risking money.

portfolio.title: Review a simulated portfolio
portfolio.description: Track virtual cash, holdings, orders, and simulated gains or losses in one place. This helps connect individual practice trades to the overall portfolio.

limitations.heading: What TradeIQ does not do
limitations.description: Clear boundaries matter when a platform deals with financial information. These limitations apply to the current build.

marketData.title: It is not a live market terminal
marketData.description: Prices are end-of-day data and may be delayed. TradeIQ shows the relevant session date where it is available.

execution.title: It does not place real trades
execution.description: Paper-trading orders use virtual money and are not routed to the Colombo Stock Exchange, a broker, or a bank account.

backtests.title: Historical results are not forecasts
backtests.description: A backtest describes how selected rules behaved under past conditions. It cannot predict future prices or guarantee a return.

signals.title: Model-driven signals are not available yet
signals.description: TradeIQ does not currently display AI predictions or model-generated trade recommendations. Planned features are not presented as working capabilities.

paperTrading.question: What is paper trading?
paperTrading.answer: Paper trading is simulated trading with virtual cash. You practise choosing a security, order side, quantity, and order settings, but no real money or exchange order is involved.

backtesting.question: What is backtesting?
backtesting.answer: Backtesting applies a defined set of trading rules to historical prices. It can help you understand how the rules would have behaved in the selected period, including the effect of assumptions such as commissions and slippage.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No account is needed to browse public CSE market data. An account is required for personal simulations such as backtests, paper-trading orders, and portfolios.

advice.question: Does TradeIQ provide investment advice?
advice.answer: No. TradeIQ provides information, research tools, and simulations for educational use. It does not recommend that you buy or sell a security.

data.question: How current is the market data?
data.answer: TradeIQ uses end-of-day CSE market data rather than a live intraday feed. The Markets pages show the session date associated with the available prices.

trust.label: Why use TradeIQ
trust.title: Build confidence before you risk real money.
trust.description: TradeIQ brings market research, historical strategy testing and paper trading into one clear learning workspace.

market.title: Read the market clearly
market.description: Browse available CSE end-of-day prices with the session date shown.

practice.title: Practise without real funds
practice.description: Paper orders use virtual money and are never sent to an exchange.

history.title: Test rules on past prices
history.description: Backtests are historical simulations, not forecasts or investment advice.
